reviewed_by: Claude Code, implementing the operator's request to mark chats and projects high priority so Core and Butler favor them without being told
reason: Every queue where work waits for shared capacity was FIFO, a poll race or alphabetical. Chats and projects can now be marked high (PATCH chat-sessions priority, PUT engagements/{id}/priority, Butler nebula.work.set_priority). A chat inherits from the chat it reports to and from its project; forks do not. High work goes first in: host-wide provider/background/tool slots (a high request that does not fit records a waiting reservation; normal requests wait while taking a slot would leave it short; stale waiters expire after 10 s), the host pressure line (high ahead of normal, FIFO within each), the Host command queue (high first, then the existing fair order), and project worker admission (high projects admitted first and never retired to make room). Butler reads show priority and list high chats first; the Butler board leads each section with high chats. Selected: test_work_priority.py (new: inheritance, project marking, capacity preference, waiter expiry and withdrawal, host-load order, Host command order, routes, Butler tool, board order) plus the existing suites of each touched module: runtime capacity, chat runtime capacity, host load and pressure, worker admission retry, Butler home scope, idle retirement dispatch, view leases, memory API (Host commands), Butler work tools and the board.
exclusions: No UI change in this PR (priority toggles and badges come with the UI PR), so no frontend or Playwright tests. PostgreSQL variants skip locally without a server and run in CI where configured. The product knowledge index does not read docs/design/work-priority.md.
